summary: Charles Rieu was an Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics scholar. He studied at Geneva and Bonn under Lassen, Freytag, and Gildemeister. He served as Curator of Oriental Mss. at the British Museum and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

Charles Rockwell Lanman was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Yale, Berlin, Tübingen, and Leipzig under Whitney, Roth, Weber, and others. He served at Johns Hopkins (1876-1880) and held a professorship at Harvard University (1880-1926).

Charles S. Prebish is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Case Western Reserve under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. His career included posts at Pennsylvania State University (~1972-2005) and Calgary (~1999).

Charles Taliaferro is a philosophy and religious studies scholar. He studied at Goddard College, Harvard Divinity School, the University of Rhode Island, and Brown University. He served as a professor at St. Olaf College from ~1985 to 2022.

Charles Taylor is a philosopher who studied at McGill University and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at Université de Montréal (~1961-1967), McGill University as Professor of Political Science (~1961-1997), and Northwestern University (~2002).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu was a philosophy, religious studies, and sinology scholar. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952-1959) and the University of Illinois System (~1965-1969), and held a post at Ohio University (~1968-1972).

Charles Wilkins was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Kalinatha. A founding member of The Asiatic Society (1784), he held librarian posts with the East India Company, the East India Company Library, and the India Office Records.

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin was an Iranian, Sinology, and Indology scholar who studied law at the University of Liège. He directed Collège Saint-Quirin (~1861-1867) and served as Professor of Oriental Languages at KU Leuven and UCLouvain (~1867-1899).

Chatral Sangye Dorje was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Ngawang Palzang, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and Sera Khandro Dewé Dorje, and later succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. She studied at Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh universities. She served in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Thammasat University (~1973-2000).

Chen-kuo Lin is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degree at Temple University. He held posts as Professor and Distinguished Professor at National Chengchi University, alongside positions at Leiden University and the International Institute for Asian Studies.
Cheryl A. Crowley is a Japanology scholar who studied under Linda H. Chance, William R. LaFleur, Philip Boas Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.
Chhimed Rigdzin Rinpoche was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and held an attested post at Visva-Bharati University in 1997.

Chi Chen Ho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. Ho studied under traditional teacher Hsuan Hua and completed a PhD under Robert E. Buswell Jr. at the University of California, Los Angeles, where Ho also worked as a teaching assistant.
Chi-chen Wang was a sinologist who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from ~1922 to 1924. He served on the faculty at Columbia University from ~1929 to 1965.

Chi-chiang Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. Huang completed a PhD at the University of Arizona in 1986, studying under doctoral supervisor Jing-shen Tao and teacher Robert M. Gimello.

Chi-wah Chan is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman. Chan also served as a teaching assistant at CUHK.
Chie Ikeya is a historian and archaeologist who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at Cornell University in 2006, where she studied under David K. Wyatt.
Chien Y. Hsu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teacher Zhenhua and doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura and James B. Apple.

Chien-hsing Ho works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Ho held positions as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).
